assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational political-economy programme linking political institutions, state capacity, electoral incentives and fiscal policy to economic development.
assessment.attribution: Besley, Persson and Tabellini provide a coherent core of formal and empirical contributions, though the wider field has many influential contributors.
assessment.maturity: The ideas have shaped research and policy debates over several decades across political economy and development.
uncertainties: The breadth of the programme makes a sharply bounded prize citation difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-data research transformed the measurement and understanding of intergenerational mobility and the role of place and childhood conditions.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren and Friedman are central to the linked administrative-data mobility research programme.
assessment.maturity: Its empirical results have been repeatedly extended and have substantially affected public-economics research and policy discussion.
uncertainties: Some central findings and data infrastructures are relatively recent.
Attribution among the broader mobility literature remains contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The analysis of how organized interests and political incentives shape trade policy supplied a durable explanation for departures from free trade.
assessment.attribution: Grossman and Helpman form an exceptionally clear and compact attribution for the central theoretical contribution.
assessment.maturity: The framework is long established and remains a core reference for political economy of trade.
uncertainties: The empirical reach of particular lobbying mechanisms varies across institutional settings.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification fundamentally changed how economists draw credible conclusions when point identification rests on untenable assumptions.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the central originator; Tamer and Molinari made important extensions and applications.
assessment.maturity: The approach is established in econometric theory and increasingly consequential in applied work.
uncertainties: Its influence is methodological and diffuse, which can complicate a public-facing prize framing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The programme established reciprocity, fairness and inequity aversion as consequential elements of economic behaviour and institutions.
assessment.attribution: Fehr and Schmidt are strongly identified with the core model, with Falk a major experimental and empirical contributor.
assessment.maturity: The results have been tested across laboratory, field and organizational contexts over many years.
uncertainties: The relevant behavioural literature is broad and includes other plausible award recipients.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Work on allocative efficiency across firms offered a powerful quantitative account of productivity and cross-country income differences.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh, Klenow and Restuccia are central contributors to the measurement and macroeconomic interpretation of misallocation.
assessment.maturity: The framework is widely used in growth, development and industrial-organization research.
uncertainties: Inferring causal distortions from observed revenue productivity remains model- and measurement-sensitive.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Audit and correspondence studies provided unusually direct evidence on discrimination in labour markets and altered empirical practice.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan are especially associated with landmark field experiments; Charles made major complementary contributions to the economics of race and discrimination.
assessment.maturity: The design has been replicated widely and informs both research and policy.
uncertainties: Audit-study estimates identify important mechanisms but do not alone measure all forms of labour-market discrimination.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their work made enduring contributions to the economic treatment of exhaustible resources, natural capital and intergenerational sustainability.
assessment.attribution: Dasgupta and Heal are natural joint recipients for the foundational resource and inclusive-wealth perspective.
assessment.maturity: The underlying theory is mature and environmental accounting has gained substantial practical relevance.
uncertainties: The proposed discovery joins several related literatures with different empirical and normative foundations.
